title: Risky Behaviour: Substances and Road Safety
summary: What risky behaviour is, factors that increase or reduce risk, the link between substance use and other risks, road safety for pedestrians, cyclists and passengers, and making safer choices.

notes.text: Behaviour that could harm your health, safety or future, or that of others.

items: Using alcohol, tobacco, vapes or drugs.
Unsafe road use: not wearing seat belts, riding with a drunk driver, texting while crossing the road.
Unsafe online behaviour: meeting strangers from the internet, sharing private information.

rows: Easy access to alcohol and drugs
Involvement in sport, arts and clubs

notes.text: One risky behaviour often leads to another. **Alcohol and drugs** affect judgement, so people under the influence are more likely to have unprotected sex, get into fights, become victims of crime or be involved in road accidents. Mixing alcohol with medicines or other drugs is especially dangerous.
Many road deaths in South Africa are **pedestrians**, and alcohol is a factor in a large share of fatal crashes.

rows: Cross at pedestrian crossings or robots; look right, left, right again; never use your phone while crossing; wear bright or reflective clothes at night; walk facing oncoming traffic where there is no pavement
Wear a helmet; use lights and reflectors at night; ride on the left with the traffic; signal before turning
Always wear a seat belt, also in the back seat and in taxis; never get into a car with a driver who has been drinking; do not distract the driver

notes.label: The law
notes.text: The legal blood-alcohol limit for ordinary drivers is **0,05 g per 100 ml** of blood (0,02 g for professional drivers). It is illegal to use a hand-held phone while driving, and all occupants must wear seat belts.

items: Think about the consequences before acting.
Plan ahead: arrange a safe lift home before you go out.
Stick with friends who look out for you.
Say no assertively and walk away from danger.
Ask for help: Substance Abuse Helpline **0800 12 13 14**; emergency services **10177** (ambulance) and **10111** (police); from a cellphone, **112**.

questions.prompt: Give THREE safety rules for pedestrians.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): use crossings; look right, left, right; no phone while crossing; bright clothes at night; walk facing traffic; do not walk on highways

questions.prompt: Your friend's older brother has been drinking and offers you a lift home. What should you do and why?
questions.memo:
✓ Refuse the lift; arrange another safe way home / call a parent (1)
✓ Alcohol impairs driving and greatly increases the risk of a crash (1)

questions.prompt: Give TWO safety rules for cyclists.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): helmet; lights and reflectors; ride on the left with traffic; signal; obey road signs
